headline: Hynix's 'sold out through 2029' extends the AI relief into memory, but desks call it supply abating, not fresh buying, and crowded test/HDD longs (TER, STX) got punished on beats into MSFT/GOOGL tonight.
market_read: Desks moved from 'is the 26 Oct bounce real?' to 'how much re-risking is left?'. GS (Marson, 28 Oct) and JPM's TMT trader (Heavey, 28 Oct) see financing fears clearing (META, SPCX, the AVGO SPV, the Anthropic S-1) but describe the buying as supply abating with tentative re-risking. UBS (Dwyer, 28 Oct) sees only a marginal buy skew, and MS (Wigg, 27 Oct) hears 'wait' from clients. Memory leadership changed hands: SK Hynix's claim that DRAM/HBM is effectively sold out through 2029, with >50% of 2027-28 under LTAs (Jefferies Titu, 28 Oct), lifted MU/SNDK pre-market. The same night, crowded beat-and-raise names fell: STX about -6% and TER about -6% after hours (UBS Ruple, 27 Oct). Crowding is rotating out of CRWV/GOOG/AMD/TER and into APP/CSCO/ON/KLAC on UBS's quant screen (27 Oct), while GOOGL bogeys stay far above Street despite negative Search chatter (BofA, Barclays, 28 Oct).

up.why: Yesterday's 'neglected, improving' name has now printed: OP KRW83.3tn, about 8% above consensus, DRAM/HBM 'effectively sold out' through 2029 and ~KRW100tn of FY26 returns vs ~KRW40tn expected (Jefferies Titu, 28 Oct). The stock was +10% and was rewarded (GS Marson, 28 Oct). monitor.json had it at HOT 61.4 (60–<80 band; own analogs h5 median +2.1%, h10 +4.3%, n=13) before the print. For 1-5 days, Samsung's print tomorrow is the next test. For 2-4 weeks, it depends on whether LTA pricing headlines hold.
up.confirm: Samsung (29 Oct) confirms tight HBM/DRAM and LTA coverage; MU/SNDK keep the lateral; desks report real-money buying, not just covering.
up.weaken: Samsung guides capacity adds or softer HBM pricing; GS/UBS desks report the bounce fading as supply-abatement buying runs out.

up.why: MU is the largest-notional pre-market mover on the Hynix read-across (+3.6%, ~$0.8bn; Jefferies Favuzza, 28 Oct), with SNDK/MU +4% (TMTB, 28 Oct). This answers Barclays' 27 Oct point that memory bulls lacked a catalyst. monitor.json: HOT 40.9 / BULL 56.6 (both 40–<60), so attention is not yet stretched; own BULL-band analogs h5 median +4.8%, h10 +8.3% (n=25). These are history, not a forecast.
up.confirm: US memory holds its pre-market gain through the MSFT/GOOGL capex prints; Samsung confirms.
up.weaken: Hyperscaler capex disappoints, or the move fades intraday as STX/TER-style 'sell the beat' spreads to memory.

up.why: MS sales (Amerian, 28 Oct): 2Q OP of 266bn vs BBG consensus of 218bn, FY guide raised to 967bn, and a buyback. CPU test is pitched as a third growth layer alongside GPU and ASIC. This contrasts with TER's crowded-long sell-off, so the test narrative is consolidating in Advantest. No HOT/BULL analog in monitor.json for this name, so the call rests on desk evidence alone.
up.confirm: Tokyo trading holds the gain; more desks repeat the CPU-test framing; the TER call fails to stabilise its peer.
up.weaken: The Advantest gain fades in line with TER, which would point to sector de-crowding rather than share shift.

up.why: UBS quant crowding +4.32 over 2 weeks, plus more analog inquiries after TXN (Ruple, 27 Oct). TXN still leads monitor.json's Bloomberg X risers (z 2.46). But NXPI's guide miss drags ON -1.7% pre-market as a lateral (Jefferies, 28 Oct), so interest is rising into a mixed analog tape. No analog row for ON.
up.confirm: The analog bid survives NXPI; MCHP/ON hold crowding gains on the next UBS screen.
up.weaken: NXPI's auto/industrial guide reads across, and analog interest reverts to TXN-only.

up.why: The UBS quant screen shows a +6.99 2-week long-crowding spike, which the desk calls the most noteworthy move in hardware/networking (Ruple, 27 Oct). This is quant data only, with no supporting desk anecdote this window, hence low conviction. No analog row.
up.confirm: Desk anecdotes of networking rotation into CSCO; the next UBS screen holds the gain.
up.weaken: The crowding gain reverses as AI networking leaders (ANET/optical) recover.

down.why: Yesterday's 'excessive popularity' name (JPM survey +5) fell about 6-7% after hours on a smaller beat. UBS still sees 'a decent amount of crowding' (Ruple, 27 Oct), and JPM says investors treated the dip as buyable but the crowded long base is vulnerable (Meyers, 27 Oct). monitor.json: HOT 51.9 / BULL 49.9; own HOT-band analogs h10 median +4.6% (n=26). The 1-5 day setup is a crowded-long flush. Over 2-4 weeks, Dec-Q exabyte staging is the swing factor.
down.confirm: STX does not reclaim the after-hours drop despite WDC/memory strength; desks report long-only selling.
down.weaken: Dip buyers step in (JPM's 'buyable' read) and STX closes the gap with WDC within a few sessions.

down.why: Beat-and-raise but -6% after hours, versus an ~11% implied move. UBS says it was more crowded than appreciated, and the UBS quant screen already showed long crowding -5.15 over 2 weeks (Ruple, 27 Oct). This diverges from Advantest's rewarded beat. No analog row for TER.
down.confirm: TER lags Advantest/semicaps through the week; crowding falls again on the next UBS screen.
down.weaken: Upbeat '27 call commentary (UBS flags the call as more relevant to price) reverses the after-hours move.

down.why: Largest 2-week long-crowding drop in the UBS tech quant screen (-8.32, 1 SD; Ruple, 27 Oct). monitor.json has Bloomberg X attention easing (Δz -2.23) with HOT 71.4 (60–<80) and weak own analogs (BULL-band h5 median -8.2%, n=15; HOT n=4, too thin). Bernstein (27 Oct) sizes $18-42bn still to raise. Long crowding is coming off even as the AI tape recovers.
down.confirm: CRWV lags the neocloud/semis bounce; more funding headlines.
down.weaken: Financing-clearing relief (META/SPCX/AVGO) extends to neoclouds and short covering lifts CRWV.

down.why: The Dec-Q guide missed both Street and the buyside bogey (~$3.9bn). The stock is -7% after running +12% into the print against a SOXX down 6% (Jefferies Favuzza, 28 Oct), so the light-positioning re-rating case Barclays laid out on 27 Oct did not happen. No analog row.
down.confirm: NXPI fails to recover on the 30 Oct BofA IR fireside; analog peers (ON) keep lagging.
down.weaken: Buyers treat the guide as conservative given the low-teens multiple, and the stock closes the move within days.

down.why: Barclays (Kantrowitz, 28 Oct) says sentiment leans negative on weak third-party Search checks, and UBS quant crowding is -5.01 over 2 weeks. But buyside bogeys stay far above Street (Cloud +101% vs 91%, 2027 EPS $18.71 vs $15.47; BofA Franco, 28 Oct), and JPM sees the OCI/OpenAI TPU news as positive. That divergence is why conviction is low into tonight's print. monitor.json: HOT 53.1 / BULL 43.6.
down.confirm: A Search print at the low end of 14-16%, or Cloud below the ~100% buyside bogey.
down.weaken: Cloud/TPU upside validates the buyside bogeys and short covering follows.

themes.title: Supply abatement, not fresh demand
themes.text: GS (Marson, 28 Oct), JPM TMT trading (Heavey, 28 Oct) and UBS (Dwyer, 28 Oct) agree the AI rebound is short covering and absent sellers after one of the largest tech liquidations on record. Re-risking is described as 'tentative' and 'barely begun'. 22V (DeBusschere, 27 Oct) argues the Anthropic S-1 makes the build-out 'hard to short'. MSFT/GOOGL tonight and AMZN tomorrow decide whether covering turns into buying.

themes.title: Sell the crowded beat: TER/STX vs Advantest/Hynix
themes.text: Beats were rewarded where positioning was light (Hynix, Advantest, FLEX) and sold where longs were crowded (STX, TER), per UBS and JPM desk reads (27 Oct). The test split, Advantest beat-and-raise up and TER beat-and-raise down, is the cleanest positioning tell this window.

themes.title: Crowding map rotates (UBS quant, Bernstein)
themes.text: UBS's biweekly quant screen (to 23 Oct) shows the biggest long-crowding drops in CRWV, GOOG, TER, AMD and MRVL and rises in APP, CSCO, ON and KLAC. Bernstein (28 Oct) finds software uncrowded overall but SNOW the most crowded name, and ORCL near the least-crowded end. These are data-derived screens, not desk opinion.

themes.title: Independent bear voice: lab financing
themes.text: Socratic Loop (independent Substack, 27 Oct; written before the S-1) is 'increasingly concerned' that independent-lab financing could cap incremental infrastructure spend. It says the S-1 added both supporting and offsetting evidence it is still debating. Kept visible as the counterweight to the desk relief narrative. No ticker-level claim, so there are no observations.

coverage_gaps: No DAMNANG or SemiAnalysis mail in this window: DAMNANG's 27 Oct piece was already logged on 27 Oct, and only a TMTB podcast note relayed SemiAnalysis.
Samsung (29 Oct) and the MSFT/GOOGL/NOW/KLAC prints tonight fall after this window; their desk reaction comes tomorrow.
Analog rows exist only for names in monitor.json's analog set: ADVANTEST, ON, CSCO, TER and NXPI have no HOT/BULL history.
monitor.json inputs predate today's rebuild (prices/Bloomberg X through 26 Oct); the page rebuild refreshes them.
source_notes: Channel outlook-com via desk_mail_collect.ps1; inbox lag 0 h; 1001 messages screened, 330 bodies pulled and ~46 read in full or in part (desk senders first). Messages up to about 13:10Z on 27 Oct were already covered by the 27 Oct review and were not re-logged.

Desk and specialist-sales voices carry no ratings or PTs. Bernstein's crowding piece and the UBS quant screens are data or research, not desk opinion. TMT Breakout and Socratic Loop are independent Substacks.
Weighting is editorial: data-derived crowding screens and multi-desk agreement weigh more than single-desk colour, and pre-market moves are logged as tape, not as conviction.
